title: Maple Hollow Rising
premise: Lior Halloran has spent a decade keeping Maple Hollow's bookshop—and their heart—carefully contained, raising their daughter Wren alone after the best mistake of their twenties, Juniper Vale, left town to chase an architecture career. When a freak snowstorm traps Lior, Juniper, and Wren in the shop overnight, old wounds and older tenderness resurface just as Juniper returns as lead architect on a development that would demolish Main Street, including the bookshop. Over the weeks leading to Maple Hollow's winter festival, Lior must choose between fighting the development that could secure the town's future on their terms or trusting Juniper, who is quietly redesigning the project to save the street. At the festival, Juniper publicly unveils the revised plans and asks for a second chance; Lior chooses love, and the bookshop becomes the heart of the new development.
about_author: Tamsin Crane is the pen name of a former small-town bookseller who now writes love stories set in places where everyone knows your coffee order. She lives with her partner, two cats, and an ever-growing stack of festival-themed romance drafts.

chapters.title: The Weight of Snow
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Opening on a quiet December morning, Lior closes up the bookshop while Wren does homework in the reading nook, establishing the careful routines that keep their life stable. News breaks that Vale Development has bought the old mill property. The beat: dread beneath routine, the past knocking at a door Lior thought was locked.

chapters.title: Juniper, In the Doorway
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper arrives in Maple Hollow to survey the site, telling herself this is strictly business, and walks into the bookshop for a permit signature. Ten years of silence collapse when she sees Lior—and a child with her own hazel eyes. The beat: shock, guilt, and the first crack in her professional armor.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A sudden snowstorm strands Juniper overnight in the shop with Lior and Wren. Power flickers, they share soup and stale gingerbread, and Wren innocently asks if Juniper is the 'J' in the old letters Lior keeps in a tin. The beat: forced intimacy thawing frozen grief into something dangerously warm.

chapters.title: What the Tin Held
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Aftermath of the storm night: Lior confesses Wren's parentage is no secret to anyone but Juniper, and anger surfaces—ten years of letters returned unopened. Juniper explains the career that pulled her out of poverty and saved her family home. The beat: painful honesty, neither villain nor victim, both wounded.

chapters.title: Rival Maps
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Town meeting: Juniper presents the development plans that would raze half of Main Street, including the bookshop. Lior stands up and organizes opposition on the spot. Privately afterward, Juniper admits she never saw the full site plan until now. The beat: public rivalry masking private longing, stakes made concrete.

chapters.title: Wren's Winter List
chapters.summary: Wren's POV (childlike third person). Wren, determined to get her two favorite adults talking, engineers a 'festival prep' errand list that keeps trapping them together—stringing lights, baking for the bake sale, choosing the festival book. Small kindnesses accumulate. The beat: found family forming in real time, hope sneaking past defenses.

chapters.title: The Almost
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Late night in the shop after inventory, surrounded by paper lanterns for the festival, Lior and Juniper nearly kiss—then Lior pulls back, refusing to be a chapter in someone else's story again. Juniper leaves in the snow. The beat: yearning cresting into heartbreak, the cost of self-protection made vivid.

chapters.title: Deadline at the Mill
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper's firm threatens to replace her unless she delivers the demolition plan by festival day. Instead she secretly works nights redrawing the project around Main Street, risking the career that once saved everything. Lior discovers her blueprints by accident. The beat: sacrifice revealed, duty inverted into devotion.

chapters.title: Festival Fire
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Climax at the winter festival: the firm's representative arrives to force the original plan, and Juniper publicly presents her revised design—with the bookshop as its anchor—gambling everything. Lior must speak for it before the town council votes. The beat: courage, public vulnerability, love declared through action rather than words.

chapters.title: Maple Hollow Rising
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Weeks later: the council approved Juniper's design, and construction begins with the bookshop intact at its center. Juniper signs a lease on the apartment above the shop. Wren hangs a new letter in the tin—this one addressed to both of them. The beat: quiet joy, memory transformed from wound to foundation, home redefined.
